io_driver_functions.notes: Raw DMA3-style bit-serial transfer primitive; disables/restores an IRQ-enable-like flag around the transfer; programs source/dest/bit-count+enable-bit then busy-waits. Also used for writes (serves both directions depending on caller's src/dst args). EEPROM MMIO literal 0xD000000 is directly visible as a constant argument in callers; the DMA3 control-register identification itself is inferred from the standard GBA hardware idiom, not from resolved literal register addresses in this decompilation.
EEPROM block READ: serializes READ opcode (0b11) + 6-bit block address, transmits via FUN_0803faf0, then clocks in 68 bits (4 dummy + 64 data) from 0x0D000000 and unpacks into 4x16-bit output words.

EEPROM block WRITE: serializes WRITE opcode (0b10) + 64 data bits + 6-bit address, transmits via FUN_0803faf0 to 0x0D000000, then busy-polls bit0 of the EEPROM status word in a timed retry loop waiting for the internal write cycle to finish. No caller found anywhere in the 248-function traced callgraph (reachable only via the FUN_0803fc20 wrapper, which is itself uncalled in this trace).
Thin wrapper forcing FUN_0803fc34's blocking/retry mode argument to 1.
Write-verification: reads back the just-written block via FUN_0803fb70 and compares all 4 words against the expected buffer; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on first mismatch.

Top-level committer: up to 3 attempts of (blocking write via FUN_0803fc20, then verify via FUN_0803fd94), breaking early on success. No caller found anywhere in the traced 248-function callgraph -- the higher-level game-state serializer that would call this is not present in the supplied decompilation.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If genuine magic/validity check: save rejected on load or backup block substituted. If incidental constant: no observable change. No checksum repair needed since none was found/proven (section 4.2 of report).

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If redundancy hypothesis correct: game falls back to an intact mirror and loads an older generation. If wrong: save treated as fully corrupt regardless of mirrors.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If pure bookkeeping counter: no visible break. If this value participates in an unidentified checksum (falsifying section 4.2's 'none found' conclusion): save rejected/reset on load.

open_questions: No caller of FUN_0803fdec (top-level EEPROM write+verify+retry) or FUN_0803fc34/FUN_0803fc20 (raw write) exists anywhere in the supplied 248-function ghidra/callgraph.json trace -- the actual game-state serializer and its RAM struct address are not present in this decompilation.

No checksum/CRC function was found anywhere in ghidra/decompiled.c; brute-force sum8/xor8/complement search over every contiguous byte range of the mutated region against both .sav samples found zero non-trivial matches. Whether a checksum exists at all for this title's save format is UNKNOWN.
Only 2 .sav samples and 0 paired .ss save states were available in this workspace, so field semantics (what each changed byte means to the game) cannot be correlated to any observed gameplay state.

The backup/mirror-slot hypothesis for blocks at 0x10, 0xa8, and 0x140 is based on a single observed transition (only block 0 changed); it is unconfirmed whether these blocks are ever rewritten under different conditions (e.g. periodic sync, explicit backup-save action).

The DMA3 MMIO register identification for FUN_0803faf0's _DAT_0803fb60/64/68 pointers is inferred from the standard GBA hardware idiom (disable IRQ, program SAD/DAD/CNT, poll busy bit) but the literal register addresses are not resolved as numeric constants in this decompilation, so it is CONFIRMED_STATIC by structure only, not by literal address match.
